name: reasoning
description: Nine human cards; named theorem obligations on the position stack. Only current state, board predicates and the popped sigil determine transitions.

routines.label: Nine cards and explicit working memory

states.label: Choose the theme
states.description: Choose a forcing move that establishes one of the eight known tactical themes.

states.label: Collect the promised material
states.description: Take the target named by the plan, or finish its capture exchange. Mate comes first.

states.label: Advance the theme
states.description: Perform the next forcing idea: renew the alignment, chase the defender, or combine check and another threat.

states.label: Answer the counter
states.description: Recover the promised material, answer check, or finish the exchange within the plan.

states.label: Save our attacked piece
states.description: Remove the attacker, defend the piece, or move it. Against a cheaper attacker, prioritize escaping with another threat.

states.label: Opponent answers check
states.description: Inspect every legal check evasion: captures, counterchecks, king moves, then remaining moves.

states.label: Opponent saves the target
states.description: Inspect the defenses relevant to the chosen threat: mate defenses, defender moves, reinforcement, or forcing counterplay.

states.label: Opponent counters the win
states.description: Inspect the checks and concrete capture exchanges still allowed by this stage of the plan.

states.label: Opponent gets one last chance
states.description: Only after no forcing counter remains: inspect safe attacks on non-pawn pieces, once per whole puzzle.

theorems.label: Clear a bound attacking line with check
theorems.statement: Move our own blocking piece with check, capture the bound back piece after every evasion, complete one necessary recapture exchange, and answer at most one final countercheck.
reply_obligations: Checks and captures elsewhere that erase the objective
theorems.scope: A quiet counter-capture may close at an existing winning_recapture_available witness. That is an immediate material-recovery certificate, not a guarantee of post-recapture mate safety. Final actual boards are checked against one further legal ply, with no extension if that finite endpoint fails.

theorems.label: Check, collect, or renew a bound skewer
theorems.statement: Check with a king-and-piece skewer. Collect an exposed loose piece; if a piece interposes, capture it with check and renew the skewer after its recapture. Stop when every legal evasion leaves the bound target attacked, undefended, and sufficient by material projection.
continuation: equal-piece exchange when the interposer capture is declined

phases: loose capture or checking interposer capture
one countercheck or every interposer-check evasion
one answer or renewed skewer or equal-piece exchange
certificate covers the renewed-skewer evasion and target capture
proof_shape.generated_conclusion: At the renewed skewer, inspect all generated legal child facts; do not count those unselected boards as explored.

reply_obligations: One countercheck after actual loose-piece collection
theorems.scope: The renewed-skewer certificate is static: it proves the bound target remains attacked and undefended with sufficient projected material. The Oracle uses attack geometry, not a future legal-capture/post-capture-safety proof. The certificate is applied only at this named finite conclusion, never to an empty generic reply card.

theorems.label: Deflect the defender screening a loose back piece
theorems.statement: Take the bound target or its extra defender, force the screening defender away, then capture the exposed back piece. A counter-capture has a separate finite checking-exchange compensation proof.
continuation: checking double attack with mate threat

phases: counter-capture compensation: two checking exchanges, a checking double threat, then at most three captures

theorems.scope: The omitted sole-defender replies have the existing one-capture material witness, not a full safety proof. Relative material gain is measured from the starting board. Each retained counter follows one fixed finite branch; no generic move search resumes.

theorems.label: Chase a bound sole defender at most three times
theorems.statement: Safely attack the sole defender of a loose piece. If it moves while preserving that defense, renew the attack twice at most. Collect the loosened target or captured attacker; answer a countercheck once without abandoning another loose piece.
theorems.scope: The existing relational defender-chase witness supplies the omitted-reply partition. All checks are retained, including checks with more than two evasions. There are exactly three attack phases and no restart of the chase after collection.

theorems.label: Threaten mate and a loose piece together
theorems.statement: A move threatens mate while attacking a loose nonpawn. Against every actual mate defense, collect the material with a forcing check or continue at most two checks that confine the king to interpositions.

phases: every check evasion if material is not yet sufficient
every final evasion and exact mate witness

theorems.scope: Actual mate-in-one endings use an exact legal-child witness. A checking material collection closes only at the finite immediate-mate/material-capture guard; it need not enumerate harmless interpositions. Two continuation checks are the maximum, even if another general attacking idea exists.

theorems.label: Repair the back-rank entry with check before collecting
theorems.statement: When taking a loose piece would abandon a back-rank entry, first check with the move that newly defends that same entry. After every check evasion, take the loose piece.

phases: check that defends the bound entry

theorems.scope: The existing compound entry binds the prospective capturer, target, vulnerable entry and added defender. The finite ending rejects immediate mate or an objective-erasing capture. A further noncapturing checking invasion is beyond this three-ply plan; the added defender is the board-facing reason the immediate mate is gone.

theorems.label: Overload a pinned target and attack its reinforcement
theorems.statement: Add a safe surplus attacker to a defended pinned nonpawn. If a defender is added, attack both the pinned piece and another loose piece; otherwise collect the pinned target. Complete one material exchange and answer one final check.
theorems.scope: The surplus must be against a defended nonpawn. The saving-reply partition is bounded. Each material collection ends only after immediate mate and objective-erasing captures are excluded; noncapturing checks after the final answer do not reopen the proof.

theorems.label: Check, collect, then repair the attacked piece once
theorems.statement: Check while safely attacking a loose nonpawn, then collect it after every evasion. First answer immediate checks and material-erasing captures. Only when none exists, spend one last-chance card per puzzle on safe counterattacks; repair the attacked piece and stop.

phases: forcing reply OR one budgeted last chance
one check answer OR one liability repair

theorems.scope: The last-chance budget is global to the puzzle, never refunded, and spent only after the forcing/material reply card finds nothing. A successful quiet repair closes that attacked-piece liability with the material objective intact and no immediate mate or recapture of the moved piece. It does not reopen every future capture of a different defended piece.

scope.label: Material finish
scope.scope: Relative gain survives every immediate capture and mating reply. Further noncapturing checks are outside this finite conclusion.

scope.label: Discharge reply
scope.scope: No matching reply remains for this named obligation. Omitted legal moves are limited by the theorem's declared reply partition; this is not unrestricted minimax.

scope.label: Clearance
scope.scope: One bounded alignment exchange, immediate material gain, or an existing winning-recapture witness; the latter alone does not establish post-recapture mate safety.

scope.label: Skewer
scope.scope: Immediate material recovery or renewed skewer geometry with sufficient projected target value. The projected capture is not a searched legal-capture-and-safety continuation.

scope.label: Overload exchange
scope.scope: The completed exchange preserves the relative gain without a further countercheck.

scope.label: Compensation
scope.scope: After a collection, all generated check evasions retain the objective, or the reached board retains it without a hanging piece attacked by a cheaper piece.

scope.label: Chase finish
scope.scope: A legal objective recapture of a loose checking piece leaving other nonpawns defended, a final nonchecking objective board, or the existing winning-recapture witness.

scope.label: Last chance
scope.scope: The selected rescue retains the goal, permits no immediate mate or recapture of the moved piece, and is not an unresolved checking continuation.
